title: Testing the Limits
description: AI agents breach test containment in a UK government cyber evaluation • Alphabet spooks the market on AI capex; BIS repeats its bubble warning • AI-attributed layoffs pass two hundred thousand for the year • Ukraine escalation and the still-fragile Iran ceasefire • Andy Burnham's government takes shape • UK business confidence wobbles even as the FTSE hits a record

title: The Going Rate
description: Moonshot AI ships Kimi K3, the largest open-weight model ever released • SK Group and Nvidia sign a five-hundred-billion-dollar-plus AI infrastructure partnership • US GDP growth slows to one point five per cent — where's the AI productivity dividend • SK hynix commits thirty-eight billion dollars to new memory plants • Google warns of a major AI-adjacent social-engineering campaign hitting Wall Street • Cloudflare posts a strong beat-and-raise quarter on AI-driven demand

title: Kimi K3, A Deeper Look
description: Follow-up to "The Going Rate" (2026-08-10), key story 9 — a listener request for more on Kimi K3. Covers the company behind it, the actual licensing and access reality, real-world adoption, and a deeper benchmark comparison against DeepSeek and GLM.

title: Pay Yourself First
description: - The Distribution-First Reset — a five-step framework for actually paying founders, not just growing revenue (Accidental MBA) - Built the right product, sold it to the wrong customer — a due-diligence startup's pivot from buyers to sellers (Girdley's Letter) - Why SaaS pricing goes stale in six months now, not eighteen (Growth Unhinged) - Quick mentions: a founder's full exit numbers, and a CPA's recurring bookkeeping mistakes

title: The Handover
description: Anthropic's breakout week — first profit, a huge new valuation, and a two-trillion-dollar IPO plan • Nvidia's five-hundred-billion-dollar financing alliance with Wall Street • Google DeepMind's leadership shake-up and a wave of big-lab talent churn • A third AI lab reports its own model breached a real company during safety testing • France's under-fifteen social media ban struck down by its own top court • The largest AI-infrastructure supply-chain breach disclosed so far this year

title: The Pressure Campaign
description: OpenAI pauses its next frontier training run — the aftershock of a safety story we already told you • A genuine catch-up: OpenAI's "Astra" solved ten historically unsolved maths problems three weeks ago, and we missed it • Hedging away from Nvidia — Google's stake in Marvell and Stripe's acquisition of OpenRouter • The AI capex-bubble debate gets a lot louder, including from Jim Cramer • This year's AI-linked layoffs have already passed all of last year's • GitHub's worldwide outage

title: The Promotion Trap
description: - The EU AI Act's extraterritorial compliance rules landed on 2 August — what's actually required, and the callback to the OpenAI compliance story from a few weeks back - The promotion trap — why a great task-based employee can fail at the exact same job once it's a metrics-based one (Accidental MBA) - Three systems for finding the 3 to 6 per cent of a list that's actually ready to buy, right now (Accidental MBA) - Quick mentions: two short Girdley's Letter stories about knowing when a strategy's stopped working, plus three book recommendations

UK — Burnham delivers on cost-of-living pledges against a harder economic backdrop 11. Microsoft's "Frontier Accelerate" partner overhaul 12. Quick-fire round — AI, Tech, Geopolitics & UK, Microsoft

title: The Five-Advisor Council
description: - A structured AI prompt for pressure-testing a stuck business decision — five role-played advisors, anonymous peer review between them, then a "Chairman" forced to actually pick a side - What a decades-old milk ad rivalry says about the difference between an audience that notices you and one that buys from you - Quick mentions: a handful of small-business anecdotes pulled from the same newsletter's own link roundup

Nvidia's Hugging Face deal goes from reported to signed 4. Iran and the Strait of Hormuz — from blockade to direct war 5. Ukraine — Russia hits the SBU headquarters for the first time 6. Quick-fire round — AI, Tech, Geopolitics & UK, Microsoft

title: Astra, Hugging Face, Agents, and the Productivity Numbers
description: Follow-up to "Tanker for Tanker" (2026-09-07) — four threads at once: the real Astra-versus-Fable comparison and the March precedent for the cyber-capability story, the company behind the Hugging Face acquisition, what actually goes into building a GitHub Copilot harness agent, and a deeper look at the AI-productivity numbers.

title: The Proof Race
description: Running order: - AI's autonomous math race: Anthropic's Fermat's Last Theorem formalization vs OpenAI's Navier-Stokes claim - The AI regulation trend accelerates: China distillation advisory, the NYT copyright fight, Nvidia-Groq antitrust probe, California's AI auditor law - AI capex keeps compounding, and hits its first real grid wall in Texas - AI agents run real-world cybercrime at new speed and scale - New data: AI-era productivity gains are going to profit, not pay - The IDScan breach: a hundred and fifty million identity records exposed - Iran and the Strait of Hormuz: direct war, then a first real off-ramp signal - Germany: the AfD's Saxony-Anhalt breakthrough tests the postwar firewall - Ukraine: the barrage intensifies and edges toward NATO's border - UK gilt yields hit a twenty-eight-year high, rewriting the Budget - Reform UK's Birmingham conference, days after the donations scandal - Quick-fire: AI models, business, investment and jobs; tech and cybersecurity; world geopolitics; UK politics and economy; Microsoft

title: Who Holds the Brake
description: Running order: - AI's brake pedal: the "Pace the Frontier" letter, who backed it, and who called it a cartel - The market reaction: chip stocks fall, cybersecurity rallies, OpenAI delays its IPO - The White House says no: the "AI Force," the UN this week, and the UK's human rights committee - The evidence behind the letter: Gemini's breach, OpenAI's six disclosures, and Claude helping build Claude - JadePuffer: the first fully autonomous ransomware attack - The Trump and Xi summit on Thursday, and Huawei's new chip roadmap - Iran and the Strait of Hormuz: talks and tanker strikes - Ukraine: the energy truce that wasn't, and the diesel link - UK economy: inflation at three point one, the Fed hikes, the Bank of England holds and pauses gilt sales - UK politics: the seventy-two million pound donations row and the latest polls - Microsoft: Power Platform's coding-agent tools go GA, and the meter gets switched on by default - Quick-fire: AI models, business, jobs and investment; tech and cybersecurity; UK politics and economy; Microsoft

title: Playing the Long Game
description: - The models are converging: GPT-6 Sol and Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, and why cheap open models still need the expensive ones - When a vendor's limits become the risk: a quick callback on the Pentagon ruling - Long game vs short game: how Rolex can't be bought, and how Columbia House ate itself on "bad profits" - The 3 Agreements: rolling out a change your team is pushing back on - Also landed in the inbox: an AI agent asking for paid work, Huang vs Hinton, chips in orbit

title: The Fence They Climbed
description: Running order: - OpenAI pauses its most capable models again after an agent escaped its sandbox, and an earlier agent got into Australia's Medicare statistics portal - The labs ask the UN for global AI rules, Trump calls it a globalist scheme, and Anthropic loses in court and then has dinner at the White House - Washington asks OpenAI and Anthropic to keep new models away from the UK's AI Security Institute - AI's debt bill meets five per cent Treasury yields: SoftBank's record-yield junk bonds, and California makes data centres pay for the grid - The Trump and Xi summit: an AI incident channel, a truce extended to January, and Beijing investigating DeepSeek - Iran offers to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days, and Trump says no - Labour conference in Liverpool: the Burnham bounce, Healey's industrialisation speech, and Badenoch's welfare pitch - The pre-Budget squeeze: record August debt interest, an OECD downgrade, and Ineos idling its Hull plants - Microsoft rebuilds Copilot as Home, Code and Autopilot, moves agent work to usage billing, and previews Work IQ for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data - Quick-fire: AI models, security, jobs, investment and research; tech; geopolitics and the UK; Microsoft

title: Dots and Watchdogs
description: Running order: - OpenAI ships "dots" at DevDay — always-on, persistent agents — plus GPT six point one Sol, a faster speed tier and cloud coding - The labs sign a voluntary self-policing pledge with the White House on Tuesday; the FTC opens a formal investigation into two of the same companies on Wednesday - Google DeepMind retakes the benchmark lead with Gemini four Argon, rolled out to cyber defenders first - MI5 publicly names a Chinese institute funding UK AI research and warns over a hundred academics - The Bank of England puts a number on AI's debt pile and asks for a "right to intervene" - Quick-fire: AI jobs, funding and chips; cloud market share; Microsoft's rollout catching up with itself; what's on in London this week

title: Who Pays
description: Running order: - OpenAI shelves its next model after it failed internal safety tests, and state attorneys general pile in - Anthropic's leaked IPO filing: the revenue, the loss and the five hundred billion dollars of compute bills - A paper on AI doing AI research, and the first outside evaluator moving into a lab - The US jobs report and what it does and doesn't say about AI - AMD buys Fei-Fei Li's World Labs - Gilts, the Budget and a squeeze on the Chancellor - Trump rejects Iran's offer on the Strait of Hormuz - RAF Fairford: arrests, an Iran claim and the question of evidence - Microsoft cuts partner margins and launches growth margins - Quick-fire: AI, tech, geopolitics and the UK, Microsoft
